statusLegend.P: definition survives this case without changing its frozen wording
statusLegend.F: case falsifies or materially misclassifies the frozen definition
statusLegend.A: classification depends on an underspecified coordinate or produces material ambiguity

A.name: Broad Potential
A.frozen: An identifiable aspect of Reality is a Resource when there is credible evidence of a non-negligible feasible path by which it could contribute to at least one bounded future state transition inside the relevant system boundary. Current possessed authority, current workload and immediate access are downstream Actionability/Option conditions.

B.name: Current Relational Affordance
B.frozen: A Resource exists only as a current relation between a specific actor/system boundary with presently possessed abilities/authority and a Reality feature that affords a class of state transitions. No current workload is required, but the enabling relation must exist now.

C.name: Conversion-Theoretic
C.frozen: Given an explicit transformation regime and composition rules, a Resource is a nontrivial element whose presence changes the reachable convertibility/composition preorder under the transformations admitted by that regime.

D.name: Option-Set
D.frozen: Relative to a specific actor/system boundary and authority/cost/risk constraints, a Resource is anything whose presence credibly enlarges that actor’s reachable future option set.

E.name: Evidenced Enrollable Potential
E.frozen: Relative to a declared actor/system boundary, a Resource is an identifiable aspect of Reality for which sufficient current evidence supports that the actor can intentionally enroll it, either now or through a bounded feasible acquisition/conversion path, as a means, input, or enabling relation for at least one admissible class of future state transitions. A current workload, current access, and possessed authority for the eventual consuming action are not required; those belong to downstream Actionable Resource/Option qualification. A mere target of action, hazard, rumor, stale artifact, or logically possible but unbounded distant usefulness is not sufficient.

r0Cases.episode: SEC EDGAR public data
r0Cases.observed: SEC submissions/XBRL are current machine-readable and require no API key, but fair-access policy, identifying user-agent rules and immutable source snapshots still govern use. Public access does not grant trading authority.
r0Cases.pressure: public information resource != unrestricted use != effect authority

r0Cases.episode: FRED high-value but gated
r0Cases.observed: FRED/ALFRED is considered high-value economic data, but current API use requires a user-held account/key authority. It remains a candidate until that authority is acquired.
r0Cases.pressure: known high-value resource != actionable resource

r0Cases.episode: Source bytes versus research evidence
r0Cases.observed: Finance requires immutable filing/source snapshots before derived research signals. The same reachable upstream data is not yet attributable evidence until exact source identity is frozen.
r0Cases.pressure: observation bytes != research-grade evidence

r0Cases.episode: Large resource universe collapses through research
r0Cases.observed: APF audit observed thousands of available resource candidates compress into a small set of information families/hypotheses, with no out-of-sample survivor and therefore no shadow/capital decision. The zero-trade outcome was valid research.
r0Cases.pressure: information abundance != hypothesis quality != capital capability; null outcomes are knowledge

r0Cases.episode: Workstation egress as Finance resource
r0Cases.observed: Finance consumes `finance-okx` as a narrow available egress capability rather than owning Surfshark nodes, resolver mechanics or tunnel generations.
r0Cases.pressure: lower-layer capability becomes a higher-layer resource; implementation should sink below consumer
r0Cases.anchor: World resource model §7; Workstation egress-pool evidence

r0Cases.episode: CC0 catalog still needs exact asset identity
r0Cases.observed: Kenney and Poly Haven are strong CC0 seeds, but site metadata/logos are not automatically covered merely because downloadable assets are CC0.
r0Cases.pressure: source/catalog label != exact resource authority/license

r0Cases.episode: Freesound is not one legal resource class
r0Cases.observed: Freesound contains CC0, CC-BY and CC-BY-NC items. Each sound's exact license determines whether it is actionable for a commercial-capable output.
r0Cases.pressure: shared source != homogeneous resource semantics

r0Cases.episode: Live Agent cognition is operational but value-unproven
r0Cases.observed: Current matched Station Zero experiments proved live DeepSeek decisions diverge materially from fixture trajectories with successful provider calls, yet additional player value remains unproven.
r0Cases.pressure: expensive capability difference != outcome/value difference

r0Cases.episode: Cheaper fixture remains a meaningful substitute
r0Cases.observed: Fixture/policy actors preserve a playable baseline and some decision structure, making them a legitimate counterfactual resource against live cognition rather than merely a test stub.
r0Cases.pressure: resources can be partially substitutable; marginal value must be measured

r0Cases.episode: Two Scenario Cases did not equal two broad experiences
r0Cases.observed: Production had two Cases, but Junction Bottleneck differed by one exact topology delta. Case count was therefore not accepted as replay/content breadth.
r0Cases.pressure: resource/content count != diversity of reachable experience states

r0Cases.episode: Existing content levers generated new research archetypes without new core
r0Cases.observed: Existing topology, pressure and placement resources were recomposed into mechanically distinct research archetypes without adding a mission factory or new World rules.
r0Cases.pressure: complementarity/composition can create capability/option value from existing resources

r0Cases.episode: Generic `resource` role was deleted from Human's minimum model
r0Cases.observed: Human M0 found that money, time, roles, rights, relationships, access and tools did not form one useful universal variable role; they were represented question-specifically as situated state/context.
r0Cases.pressure: over-broad Resource ontology can reduce explanatory power

r0Cases.episode: The same tool changes role with the question
r0Cases.observed: Human's retained dynamic model states that a tool can be context, intervention or part of a joint system depending on the study.
r0Cases.pressure: resource role is relational/question-dependent rather than intrinsic

r0Cases.episode: Model output, joint-system capability and retained Human capability diverge
r0Cases.observed: Human research treats an Agent/model as a real joint-system resource while refusing to infer that its output has become retained individual knowledge or skill.
r0Cases.pressure: resource-assisted effect != internal capability transfer

r0Cases.episode: Not all generated knowledge should consume Human attention
r0Cases.observed: AE1 allocates representations using Durability × Future Control Value plus an independent promotion gate; many Agent outputs remain external or locator-level rather than entering stable Human memory.
r0Cases.pressure: attention is scarce conversion capacity; maximum knowledge internalization/utilization is not optimal

r0Cases.episode: 415 Surfshark transport variants
r0Cases.observed: The sanitized provider catalog exposed 142 logical nodes / 415 transport variants while current Surfpath execution evidence could still be stale or unqualified. Catalog growth did not create 415 usable egress capabilities.
r0Cases.pressure: catalog cardinality != current option count != capability

r0Cases.episode: `native-a` and `native-b` can converge
r0Cases.observed: Two loopback transport profiles can exist while both descend through one native physical WAN/access domain.
r0Cases.pressure: nominal alternatives != failure-domain-independent redundancy
r0Cases.anchor: Workstation `README.md` network profiles; World resource model §4

r0Cases.episode: 98 public VPN candidates versus one admitted root
r0Cases.observed: A fresh VPN Gate directory exposed 98 candidates across many countries/operators, but physical qualification and exact admission were still required and only bounded candidates became roots.
r0Cases.pressure: candidate universe != executable resource stock

r0Cases.episode: Snowflake broker success but no shared capacity
r0Cases.observed: A pinned Tor/Lyrebird client could reach the broker and create offers while the broker reported no volunteer proxies. The resource remained known/testable but currently `UNAVAILABLE`.
r0Cases.pressure: executable client != available shared resource; capacity is separate

r0Cases.episode: Same public mechanism, different parent relation
r0Cases.observed: Direct Snowflake attempts failed in one relation while the same pinned client inside an admitted JP outpost bootstrapped and served traffic.
r0Cases.pressure: actionability is relation/path/context dependent, not intrinsic to the nominal resource

r0Cases.episode: Different roots but shared physical access
r0Cases.observed: Root A and B used different route profiles, protocols, nodes and endpoints, yet shared the same local gateway/MAC and Surfshark provider. The retained claim was graph/lifecycle diversity, not physical/provider independence.
r0Cases.pressure: diversity has dimensions; redundancy depends on relevant disturbance class

r0Cases.episode: Public observation expansion without capability expansion
r0Cases.observed: NX8 reached 24/24 current read-only resources across 12 observation owners while current capability coverage stayed 18/22 slots. More observers improved owner/mechanism/method diversity without creating new capability classes.
r0Cases.pressure: resource abundance can improve evidence robustness without increasing effect capability

r0Cases.episode: Large public datasets left indexed
r0Cases.observed: M-Lab raw data requires AUP/authenticated access; Censored Planet bulk data can impose requester-pays costs. Bounded APIs already satisfied current high-value truths, so bulk data remained indexed/query-on-demand instead of mirrored.
r0Cases.pressure: acquisition/storage/utilization can be irrational when marginal capability is zero

r0Cases.episode: Historical child resource invalidated by parent change
r0Cases.observed: A child external observation retained its own historical `AVAILABLE` fact, but stopping/replacing the parent Anchor caused current projection to become `UNKNOWN`; fresh discovery was required.
r0Cases.pressure: dependency currentness; historical truth survives while current option dies

r0Cases.episode: Failed WARP experiment becomes search memory
r0Cases.observed: A Cloudflare WARP experiment failed to realize a current usable L3 path; cleanup was exact, but the candidate was retained with a lower current-context score and explicit reconsideration triggers.
r0Cases.pressure: failed consumption can become Knowledge Resource; retirement can be conditional

r0Cases.episode: Stable consumer resource over replaceable physical members
r0Cases.observed: `finance-okx` presents a stable loopback consumer identity while Workstation owns replaceable member leases/generations underneath. A member/path may change without changing Finance's semantic resource identity.
r0Cases.pressure: abstraction boundary; stable resource contract can sit over renewable physical options

r0Cases.episode: Installed capability deliberately excluded from ambient authority
r0Cases.observed: Workstation removed stale user-scope Node/uv/PNPM paths from ambient execution authority while retaining exact installations or historical interpreters where active consumers still required them.
r0Cases.pressure: possession != ambient authority; retirement depends on dependencies, not age alone

r0Cases.episode: Public vulnerability intelligence is read-only resource, not exploit authority
r0Cases.observed: OSV, CISA KEV and NVD were machine-readable and useful for observation/prioritization while explicitly granting no authority to probe or exploit third-party systems.
r0Cases.pressure: information resource != action authority

r0Cases.episode: Provider claim and Security truth remain separate
r0Cases.observed: Security Research Corpus records provider claims, source snapshots and case evidence but does not promote an upstream classification into independent Security truth.
r0Cases.pressure: evidence resource has provenance/truth-role; ingestion != belief/knowledge promotion

r0Cases.episode: Sample metadata/materialization never grants execution authority
r0Cases.observed: A sample can be cataloged and even materialized in SampleVault while `executionAdmission` remains denied by default.
r0Cases.pressure: possession of dangerous resource != authority to consume it through execution

r0Cases.episode: Large retained sample need not be duplicated into every research store
r0Cases.observed: A retained case references an exact ~7.4 GiB archive identity/history without copying the bytes into the Git corpus.
r0Cases.pressure: local materialization/storage count != knowledge availability; references can preserve option value

r0Cases.episode: libvirt was available but intentionally deferred
r0Cases.observed: Security found legitimate feature overlap with libvirt but retained local exact QMP/process/ledger/recovery semantics because libvirt would add another state owner before deleting enough plumbing.
r0Cases.pressure: mature available tool can reduce net capability through coordination/authority cost

r0Cases.episode: Remote entitlement and remote capability are different resources
r0Cases.observed: CA-LIC experiments showed that a remote license/entitlement decision can leave the protected capability local, whereas external primitive/remote capability moves necessary secret/operation outside the client trust domain.
r0Cases.pressure: authority carrier != capability location; superficially similar resources have different causal roles

r0Cases.episode: REAPER crossed from installed tool to proven production resource
r0Cases.observed: Official REAPER 7.78 was not promoted merely because it launched. ReaScript created native project state and an independent render reconstructed an exact WAV.
r0Cases.pressure: installation != capability; native editable state + reproducible effect matters

r0Cases.episode: OBS capability without permanent listener
r0Cases.observed: OBS/obs-websocket was dogfooded through authenticated scene observe/mutate and then restored byte-exact with the websocket server disabled and no listener.
r0Cases.pressure: useful capability need not imply permanent utilization/presence; dormant resources can be safer

r0Cases.episode: Blender exit code zero with failed work
r0Cases.observed: Blender dogfood found that a Python traceback can coexist with exit code zero. Artifact/state postconditions were required before the tool counted as successful production equipment.
r0Cases.pressure: process success != semantic effect; resource consumption needs outcome evidence

r0Cases.episode: One successful equipment encounter produced only provisional medium status
r0Cases.observed: Blender and OBS established real spatial/live worlds, but Studio promoted those media only to `provisional`; mature craft profiles still require real works.
r0Cases.pressure: tool capability != domain mastery/value capability

r0Cases.episode: Figma installed/configured but OAuth consent absent
r0Cases.observed: Figma was installed and official Remote MCP OAuth initiation worked, yet user consent remained incomplete, so no design read/write capability was claimed.
r0Cases.pressure: installed/configured != possessed authority != actionable capability

r0Cases.episode: TouchDesigner remains a high-information candidate
r0Cases.observed: TouchDesigner could add a materially new realtime operator/dataflow world, but account/license authority was absent. It remained a valuable candidate rather than being installed to improve tool count.
r0Cases.pressure: option value can exist before acquisition; authority is a separate relation

r0Cases.episode: Inkscape deliberately not acquired
r0Cases.observed: Inkscape was withheld because current SVG+rsvg plus higher-information pending Figma work left little marginal information/capability gain.
r0Cases.pressure: available resource can have negative/zero marginal acquisition value

r0Cases.episode: Discovery source versus owner truth
r0Cases.observed: Aggregators, indexes and catalogs can establish that an offer/resource was observed, but not current terms, quota, eligibility, license or permission.
r0Cases.pressure: discovery != authority; candidate != actionable resource

r0Cases.episode: Required authority versus possessed authority
r0Cases.observed: World split provider requirement, acquisition desirability and current possessed authority into separate coordinates. A positive-EV gated resource can be worth acquiring while still being unusable now.
r0Cases.pressure: requirement != acquisition decision != possession

r0Cases.episode: Parent entitlement unlocks children
r0Cases.observed: One verified education/student entitlement can unlock many downstream developer offers; before the parent exists the children remain dependent acquisition candidates rather than independent usable resources.
r0Cases.pressure: prerequisite resource; complementarity; human-work compression

r0Cases.episode: Provider-specific acquisition failure
r0Cases.observed: OCI Free Tier was a legitimate high-value candidate, but the current operator payment/eligibility path was rejected by the provider. The failure was retained as OCI-specific negative acquisition evidence instead of being generalized to unrelated providers.
r0Cases.pressure: acquirable-in-theory != eligible-now; negative evidence; non-generalization

r0Cases.episode: Signup transport versus resource value
r0Cases.observed: A transient signup-page network failure is not allowed to erase the expected value of an otherwise legitimate entitlement; machine transport is qualified later when actual consumption begins.
r0Cases.pressure: access relation is time/path scoped; discovery/acquisition and machine consumption are different stages

r0Cases.episode: HTTP success versus semantic utility
r0Cases.observed: TCP/TLS/HTTP success can return error pages, stale endpoints, empty quota shells or nominal credits that do not serve a workload. World requires semantic consumption before `useful=true`.
r0Cases.pressure: reachable != useful; resource value is consumer-relative

r0Cases.episode: Historical admission versus current presence
r0Cases.observed: Resource Transfer can retain a durable destination receipt even after the native destination bytes are deleted. The receipt proves historical semantic admission, not current resource presence.
r0Cases.pressure: historical evidence != current resource state; persistence has multiple meanings

r0Cases.episode: Capability becomes a higher-layer resource
r0Cases.observed: Workstation scoped egress, Runtime contained execution and Harness cognition are capabilities at their native owner boundary but resources to Finance/Game/Security consumers.
r0Cases.pressure: Resource/Capability role is system-boundary relative

boundaryCases.scenario: Official high-value API is known and documented, but the actor has no current credential.
A credential that used to work has expired and cannot authenticate; renewal is a separate process.
A public mechanism-rich research paper is accessible, but there is no current project asking for it.
A private dataset is only rumored to exist; there is no inspectable provenance, owner confirmation or access path.
A healthy owned GPU is powered off and idle; no current workload needs it.
There are 415 nominal transport variants whose relevant outage mode is the same physical access/provider domain.
One hour of current Human attention is available.
A trusted collaborator relationship/reputation reliably enables introductions and review, but is not an owned object.
A legacy dependency creates recurring failures and maintenance burden; its presence shrinks feasible safe changes.
A malware sample is locally materialized; static analysis is authorized but execution is not.
boundaryCases.pressure: same object, bounded authority by transition class

boundaryCases.scenario: A model API is operational and changes actions, but no consuming domain has shown better Outcome.
A valid legal/license permission exists, but the corresponding tool/data bytes are not currently present.
An explicit contractual option/right can be exercised later before expiry but is currently unexercised.
A failed experiment leaves exact negative evidence and a reconsideration trigger.
A lower owner exports a stable bounded Capability that a higher owner can consume without knowing its mechanism.
An arbitrary pebble on the desk has no known Ordivon use or plausible bounded transition mechanism.
A distant asteroid contains useful minerals in principle, but Ordivon has no plausible bounded acquisition path or horizon.
A hostile botnet capability is controlled by an adversary; it can change Ordivon states only against the owner’s interests.
An unrestricted cash reserve is idle and can be allocated later across multiple domains.
Open-source tool code is available but incompatible with the current stack; adaptation is feasible with bounded work.

freshEFalsifiers.scenario: GPU waste heat can warm a room, but room heating is outside the declared Ordivon system boundary.
A stolen third-party credential technically works but its use is not owner-authorized or legally admissible.
A free API is reachable now, but provider terms prohibit the intended commercial transition while permitting unrelated personal use.
A dataset is ten years stale: valid for historical analysis but invalid for a current-state claim.
A random data corpus is accessible and can mechanically enter model training, but there is no evidence it helps any admissible capability and known tests show degradation.
freshEFalsifiers.pressure: mechanical input versus evidenced directional contribution

freshEFalsifiers.scenario: An encrypted backup exists, but its key is irretrievably lost and no bounded recovery path is known.
freshEFalsifiers.pressure: identified object without feasible conversion path

freshEFalsifiers.scenario: A formerly learned Human skill has decayed below current usable proficiency, but retained priors make bounded refresh materially cheaper than learning from zero.
freshEFalsifiers.pressure: latent reacquisition advantage versus current capability

freshEFalsifiers.scenario: A component has no standalone use and only becomes useful with a complement that is not held but is cheaply and credibly acquirable.
A theoretically useful external asset is purchasable only at a cost beyond every bounded Ordivon resource envelope.
freshEFalsifiers.pressure: technical market availability without bounded feasibility

freshEFalsifiers.scenario: A formal option exists but will expire before the actor can satisfy its prerequisites, making exercise infeasible in time.
freshEFalsifiers.pressure: nominal right without bounded temporal exercise path

deletionTests.mutation: Remove actor/system boundary and ask only whether the aspect can contribute to some transition somewhere.
deletionTests.reason: Without the actor/boundary coordinate, adversary-controlled capability and out-of-boundary utility become indistinguishable from resources available to Ordivon.

deletionTests.mutation: Replace sufficient current evidence with mere logical possibility.
deletionTests.reason: Rumored datasets and arbitrary objects become Resources merely because an imaginable use can be invented.

deletionTests.mutation: Permit any theoretically possible future conversion regardless of horizon/cost/prerequisites.
deletionTests.reason: Irretrievable, temporally impossible and economically unreachable objects collapse into the same class as realistic deferred resources.

deletionTests.mutation: Count anything that changes reachable states, including hazards and burdens.
deletionTests.reason: Liabilities, hostile capabilities and known-degrading inputs become positive Resources rather than constraints/hazards.

deletionTests.mutation: Allow vague source/category claims without identifying what object/relation the evidence is about.
deletionTests.reason: Catalog-level claims silently transfer authority/license/currentness to heterogeneous underlying items.

deletionTests.coordinate: class of future state transitions / mechanism
deletionTests.mutation: Remove the requirement for an evidenced transition class or mechanism.
deletionTests.reason: Resource becomes an uninformative synonym for background Reality.

deletionTests.mutation: Require an active workload or current concrete goal for Resource existence.
deletionTests.reason: Dormant general-purpose resources and option-bearing rights lose Resource status despite credible bounded future use.
Gated but credibly acquirable resources, references and enabling rights are confused with non-resources.

deletionTests.mutation: Require the authority needed for eventual consumption to already be possessed.
deletionTests.reason: Resource collapses toward Actionable Resource and cannot represent acquisition optionality.

deletionTests.mutation: Require evidence that use improves the final domain Outcome before something qualifies as Resource.
deletionTests.reason: Inputs with real transition potential are confused with proven value; Resource would collapse toward validated Capability/Outcome.

deletionTests.mutation: Require every Resource to have one total-order scalar value.
deletionTests.reason: Context-dependent, incomparable and option-bearing resources cannot be truthfully totally ordered.

r2ProvisionalResult.reason: A survives breadth but needs actor/directionality; B places current authority too early; C is useful conversion algebra but regime-underspecified as ontology; D is circular and portfolio-marginal. E adds only coordinates independently demanded by A falsifiers and then survives ten post-freeze fresh falsifiers.
candidateLayering: Resource Candidate = a claim/observation whose evidence is insufficient to establish E
Actionable Resource = Resource plus current owner truth/possessed authority/access/qualification for a demand
Option = demand-scoped admissible use/composition available to selection
